stem: Parents report that their toilet-trained 3-year-old has begun having occasional accidents and asking to use a bottle since a new sibling came home. Which nursing response is most appropriate?

options.A: Explain that temporary regression can occur; provide reassurance, one-on-one attention, and age-appropriate ways for the child to feel included
options.B: Tell the child to act their age and remove attention whenever regressive behavior occurs
options.C: Focus family attention primarily on the newborn so the older child learns to be independent
options.D: Begin several other major routine changes now so the child adapts to all transitions at once

rationale: AAP guidance notes that preschool children may temporarily regress after a new sibling arrives, such as having toileting accidents or wanting a bottle. Recommended strategies include giving the older child needed attention, setting aside special one-on-one time, involving the child in age-appropriate ways, and avoiding unnecessary simultaneous routine changes. Shaming, withdrawing attention, or piling on additional transitions can worsen adjustment. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Support preschool sibling adjustment to a new baby by normalizing temporary regression, maintaining individual attention, and involving the child in age-appropriate family activities.
source_document_title: Preparing Your Older Child for a New Baby: How to Help Siblings Adjust
source_locator: Preschoolers ages 2 to 4 years > After your new baby arrives: expect some regression; provide the attention needed rather than telling the child to act their age; set aside special time; invite the child to help and feel included. Before baby arrives: avoid stacking major routine changes when possible
source_claim_supported: Temporary regression can occur after a new sibling arrives, and supportive one-on-one attention and age-appropriate inclusion can help the older child adjust.

audit_findings: A matches current AAP recommendations. B uses shaming/withdrawal; C increases exclusion; D contradicts advice to avoid unnecessary simultaneous transitions. Regression is contextualized rather than automatically labeled a disorder. One best answer remains and independent adversarial second pass passed.
